system.name: MITOSIS
system.one_liner: an RDMA-codesigned remote-fork mechanism giving serverless functions fast, provisioning-free concurrency by forking process state across machines

content.subject: how a 3-function chain forks itself across machines, tracking page ownership via RDMA and per-hop page tables

elements.name: data
elements.role: list shared across all forked functions via fork, appended to by each function

elements.name: func0
elements.role: first function in the chain; the initial process before any fork

elements.name: func1
elements.role: forked child that reads data[0] from func0 and appends a new derived value

elements.name: func2
elements.role: second-hop forked child that reads data[1] from func1 and returns the final result

elements.name: data[0]
elements.role: value produced by func0 and consumed by func1, carried by the first fork

elements.name: data[1]
elements.role: value produced by func1 and consumed by func2, carried by the second fork

elements.name: DRAM
elements.role: per-hop memory holding the forked process's pages, referenced via RDMA from the previous hop

elements.name: Page Table
elements.role: per-hop page table tracking ownership of remote pages for that hop's memory

elements.name: RDMA
elements.role: labels the remote-memory-access link fetching pages across a fork hop

relations.what: RDMA read of the remote page/page table across the first hop
RDMA read of the remote page/page table across the second hop
each hop's page table tracks ownership of that hop's DRAM pages

steps.what: runs first and appends to the shared data list
forked from func0; reads data[0] over RDMA from func0's machine and appends its derived value
forked from func1; reads data[1] over RDMA from func1's machine and returns the result

content.key_idea: Tracing example code through its multi-hop remote-fork execution shows how each forked function reads the prior hop's output over RDMA from a different machine's DRAM.
content.reading_order: left code listing top-to-bottom, matched by the func0/func1/func2 tags to the chain diagram on the right, then down to each hop's RDMA/DRAM/page-table pair

palette.used_for: white fill of the code-listing box and the DRAM/Page Table boxes
blue used for the fork robot icons, func labels and the data[0]/data[1] hop arrows
pale peach fill of the DRAM boxes
pale blue fill of the Page Table boxes
small teal accent, likely a minor icon detail

style.stroke: thin (~0.11pt) black outlines on boxes; a few blue accent strokes on icons/arrows, not dashed
style.arrows: mostly plain thin black connector lines chaining code to diagram to RDMA hops, with a few curved wavy strands for the RDMA links and minimal visible arrowheads
style.font: mixed monospace Consolas for the code listing and sans PingFangSC-Semibold for labels, 4.5-6.5pt, over half bold
style.icons: one small robot/drone bitmap icon (denoting a forked function instance) reused for func0/func1/func2

encoding.color_means: blue = fork icons, function labels and the data[0]/data[1] hop arrows; pale peach = DRAM boxes; pale blue = Page Table boxes
encoding.line_style_means: solid black lines connect code to diagram and diagram nodes in sequence; wavy strands denote the RDMA link fetching a hop's remote pages
encoding.state_means: each hop is a separate icon labelled func0/1/2, so sequence position and label distinguish the hops rather than colour
encoding.marker_means: the func0/func1/func2 oval tags identify which code definition maps to which chain node; 'fork' and data[0]/data[1] labels on the connecting arrows name the operation and payload of each hop
encoding.emphasis: blue highlighting on the fork icons and hop arrows draws the eye along the chain from code to the underlying RDMA/DRAM hop for each fork
reusable_patterns: code listing paired label-for-label with an adjacent node chain, with per-hop memory boxes drawn beneath the link they belong to
weaknesses: small (4.5-6.5pt) labels and overlapping wavy RDMA strands make the per-hop DRAM/page-table correspondence hard to trace

evidence: MITOSIS supports multi-hops fork: a child can be forked again with its children
the pages behind data[1] and data[0] resides on two different machines
we dedicate 4 bits in the PTE’s ignored bits to encode the remote page machine

summary: MITOSIS gives serverless functions fast remote fork without pre-provisioned concurrency, letting a child process be forked again on a third machine to build a multi-hop fork chain. This figure traces one concrete 3-function example (func0, func1, func2) from its Python source, where each function reads a shared 'data' list, to the resulting execution chain: func0 forks func1 across data[0], and func1 forks func2 across data[1]. Matching oval labels tie each code definition to its node in the chain diagram. Beneath the chain, per-hop DRAM and Page Table boxes linked by RDMA show that each fork hop's memory lives on a different machine, and MITOSIS must track page ownership across hops (via 4 bits it dedicates in each PTE) rather than maintaining a separate ownership map, keeping the mechanism's memory overhead low.
summary_zh: 该图展示MITOSIS的多跳远程fork机制：以func0→func1→func2三函数示例，用椭圆标签把代码与调用链节点对应，并在每一跳下方画出DRAM与页表，说明通过RDMA跨机器追踪页所有权，仅用PTE中4位编码，无需额外映射表。
